goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_026) Identify and compare five mechanisms proposed to explain rising income inequality in advanced economies since 1980. For each mechanism: state the causal pathway, name a key empirical indicator, and identify one limitation of that explanation.
ground_truth: 1. Skill-biased technological change (SBTC, Katz-Murphy): automation raises relative demand for skilled workers, widening the college wage premium; limitation: cannot explain the dramatic rise of the top 0.1%. 2. Globalization (Stolper-Samuelson): trade with low-wage countries depresses wages for low-skill workers; indicator: manufacturing employment decline; limitation: trade deficits explain only part of wage stagnation. 3. Decline of unions (Freeman): union membership fell from ~35% to ~10% in US, reducing wage floors; limitation: union decline began before sharp inequality rise. 4. Winner-take-all superstar effects (Frank-Cook): media, finance, and tech markets reward top performers disproportionately; indicator: top 0.1% income share tripled; limitation: not universal across all sectors. 5. Capital vs labor share shift (Piketty r>g): rate of return on capital r exceeds growth rate g, accumulating wealth to capital owners; indicator: capital share rose across most OECD countries; limitation: r>g does not always hold historically.
